# The cross-window observation surface has no owner but the entrypoint

## Context

**This leaf is already implemented and green — it is a close-target split, not queued work.** PR #18499 has carried it since 2026-09-08 and cannot leave draft without an honest `Resolves`, because its parent #18460 needs three more Contract-Ledger rows and one of those is now blocked on #18533. #18456 requires every leaf to be *"independently reviewable and resolvable by one PR"*; #18460 as scoped is not, so the delivered row gets its own leaf and the criteria travel intact.

Filed deliberately as a split rather than by narrowing #18460 to fit the PR that exists — that would be weakening a criterion to match the work, which is the failure #18460's own 2026-09-08 prescription-correction was written to stop.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-09T10:36Z (#18533 … #18376); no equivalent found. A2A in-flight claim sweep over the last 30 messages: the only live dock claims are #18528 (@neo-opus-ada) and #18529 (@neo-opus-grace), neither overlapping. Memory Core rationale sweep on the problem's nouns surfaced the load-bearing prior decision, quoted below. Own-assignment sweep: #18460, #18027, #17918, #16212 — no overlap.

## The Problem

`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` is a ~2,500-line entrypoint in which nothing distinguishes the methods that *act* from the methods that only *watch*, so every reader re-decides that per method.

`readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot` is 70 lines of read-only projection — it aggregates semantic, rendered, arbitration and physical-park truth for one cross-window pointer frame — and **no engine code calls it**. Its production readers are `apps/workstation/tour/NativeGestureDriver.mjs` and four e2e specs; nothing under `src/` reaches it. It is pure observation living in the same class as the vessel effects it observes.

**The prior decision this must respect, and why it is not a contradiction.** @neo-gpt-emmy recorded during #18457: *"readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot remains on Workspace because live native observers use it."* That constraint is real and correct — four e2e specs invoke it across the Neural Link **by name** at seven call sites (`callMethod(workspaceId, 'readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot', […])`), and a unit spec reaches it as `Workspace.prototype.readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot.call(workspace, …)`. Both resolve against the prototype. This leaf honours the constraint by a different mechanism rather than overturning it: a mixin keeps the method on the prototype, so every existing reader resolves it unchanged.

## The Architectural Reality

- A helper module plus a delegate would satisfy a line count and reintroduce exactly the forwarding façade #18460 AC-2 forbids. The readers address the *instance* by name, so the only home preserving the contract is the prototype.
- `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.TopologySeams` is the engine's own precedent for this shape, for the same stated reason.
- The four vessel receipts (`lastVesselParkReceipt`, `lastVesselRestoreReceipt`, `tearOutParkGeometries`, `vesselConversionTargetWindowId`) **must not move with it.** Each is a stage machine its owning method amends as it advances (`identity-refused` → `route-refused` → `embodiment-refused` → `native-dispatched` → `acknowledged`), and `closeTearOutVessel` holds its receipt in a local `const` so the amendments survive re-entrancy. Relocating them would be the *"lost success or recovery claim after an await"* that #18460's Contract Ledger refuses.

## The Fix

Move `readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot` out of `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` into a `Workstation.view.CrossWindowGestureSnapshot` mixin that states why it exists, and declare it through `mixins`. The host keeps the receipts and every method that acts.

One adaptation is required and belongs in the mixin, commented: the host's `Workspace.MAIN_WORKSPACE_ID` static becomes `me.constructor.MAIN_WORKSPACE_ID`, because a mixin has no lexical binding to its host and importing the host to read one static would make the pair circular.

`.gitignore` also gains the workstation whitelist. `/apps/**/*.mjs` ignores everything and every tracked workstation file predates the rule, so git grandfathered them — a *new* file there is silently unstageable. Three negation lines, the shape every other app already carries.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot` | its actual readers: `NativeGestureDriver`, four e2e specs via Neural Link `callMethod`, one unit spec via `Workspace.prototype` | resolves unchanged on the instance and the prototype after the move | none needed — no signature, payload or call shape changes | mixin class JSDoc states why a mixin and not a module | both call shapes exercised at head; a control proves the arm is load-bearing |
| `Workstation.view.CrossWindowGestureSnapshot` | `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.TopologySeams` precedent | new mixin, ≤200 lines, declared via `mixins` | — | class JSDoc | `git grep -c` on the host returns 1, the `mixins:` docblock, not a call |

## Decision Record impact

`none`. No operation semantics, ownership boundary or ADR authority changes — the method keeps its home on the prototype and its readers keep their call shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

> **Rewritten 2026-09-09, on @neo-opus-ada's correction in her PR #18499 review:** the first version derived its criteria *from the delivered work* — a `.gitignore` clause that cannot pre-exist the change, an adaptation named by its variable, a trap citing a defect only knowable after the move. **A ticket written from the work cannot falsify the work**; those ACs could only ever return "met". These are re-derived from #18460's Contract-Ledger row 4 — *receipts and diagnostics → truthful observation at the owning boundary, no lost success or recovery claim after an await* — which is an obligation that could have failed this PR. Implementation detail moved to the PR's Test Evidence, where it belongs.

- [ ] The cross-window observation surface has a **stated owner distinct from the entrypoint**, and that owner explains why it is not a helper module. A rename, a body move, or a module plus a delegate does not discharge this: the delegate is the forwarding façade #18460 AC-2 forbids.
- [ ] **Every current reader still resolves the method unchanged** — the Neural-Link `callMethod`-by-name callers and the `Workspace.prototype…call` caller alike. This can fail: any owner that is not prototype-resolving breaks all eight call sites, which is the constraint @neo-gpt-emmy recorded on #18457 (*"remains on Workspace because live native observers use it"*).
- [ ] **No success or recovery claim is lost.** The four vessel receipts stay amendable by the methods that own them across their awaits, and the observation surface **cannot amend them** — not merely "does not". A design where the reader could write back to a receipt fails this criterion even if nothing currently does.
- [ ] **The move is proven faithful by comparison, not by a green suite.** A line-by-line diff of the relocated body against its predecessor, with every divergence named and justified. This can fail: a silent transcription defect passes every existing test.
- [ ] **Line counts are reported, and the entrypoint ceiling is not claimed.** Host before/after, replacement module, and combined — including a combined *increase* if the owner costs more than the host sheds. No replacement module exceeds 2,000 lines; #18456 owns the 1,000-line entrypoint ceiling and this leaf must not appear to discharge it.

## Out of Scope

- #18460's other three Contract-Ledger rows — view interaction, product vessel policy, and native effects/lifetime. Row 3's remainder is blocked on #18533.
- The `VesselPark` park/re-show transaction (#18533) and anything that would constitute a new generic window lifecycle or registry.
- The #18456 entrypoint ceiling, which needs the sibling leaves.

## Avoided Traps

A helper module with a one-line delegate would pass a line-count check and reintroduce the forwarding façade the parent forbids — the readers address the instance, so the module shape is the trap, not the shortcut. Moving the receipts along with the reader looks like tidying and would drop recovery claims across an await. And a green suite is not evidence the move is faithful: a hand-move of 70 dense lines already produced one silent transcription defect on this exact body, caught by diff and invisible to every passing test.
